After just 4 months in the job, calls grow for resignation of Ukraine’s veterans minister When Vitalii Kim was appointed Ukraine's new minister for veterans affairs, the decision triggered an outcry among the very people he was tasked with supporting. Three months later, criticism of his ministry continues. The controversy deepened further after an interview this week with RBC Ukraine in which Kim downplayed the importance of psychological support in veterans' recovery and said that crime in Ukraine would "definitely" increase as soldiers returned from the front. His remarks fueled further indignation, adding to growing concerns about the direction of his ministry's policies and questions over whether his appointment was driven less by the interests of veterans than by political ambiti ons. 🇪🇺 Kaja Kallas's job as EU foreign policy chief is starting to look shaky. EU leaders left her off Europe's Ukraine peace talks team after she had openly pitched herself as the envoy. Germany has proposed putting her under Ursula von der Leyen's supervision, which would effectively turn the EU's top diplomat into a Commission staffer. Von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa were asked about her and didn't say a word in her defence. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni reportedly told leaders behind closed doors that Kallas doesn't have the weight for serious negotiations. The complaints from diplomats are piling up. They say she goes off script on China and Israel and launches initiatives without asking member states, like the defence expert group that had to be scrapped in September. They also say she spent months opposing any talks with Russia, then asked to lead them. Her pitch in Dublin, "Russians don't want me," was called "clumsy." One diplomat reminded her that the job is finding the lowest common denominator among 27 capitals, not freelancing. Some commentators say the post itself is weak, because EU treaties give the foreign policy chief very little real power. But Kallas has an extra problem: neither the Commission nor the member states are backing her. She still has fans, but mostly outside Brussels, among people who like her hard line on Russia. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

The United States imposed new sanctions targeting three individuals and three entities over alleged financial links to Hezbollah, including the Wa Ta’awanu Association, a Lebanese charity providing emergency relief in southern Lebanon. The US Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) accused the association of using humanitarian services as "cover for Hezbollah activities" and alleged that it "channels outside donor funds" toward the group. The sanctions also targeted Lebanese businessman Hassan Khechen, his brother Ibrahim, and two companies linked to an alleged gold and cash "smuggling network" operating between Lebanon and Turkey: Lebanon-based Gold Global Company and Turkey-based Sankari Gold. The sanctions block the targeted parties’ assets under US jurisdiction and generally prohibit US persons from conducting transactions with them.
